hook: A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command ISR platform flying over Syria at 20,088 feet reported a series of light and glare anomalies crossing its FMV camera feed across a 45-minute window on 20 October 2024, formally logged as a UAP incident and submitted to AARO under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE.
why_it_matters: This report demonstrates the institutionalization of UAP reporting within active USCENTCOM counterterrorism operations, with a field crew submitting a structured AARO-format incident report mid-mission while continuing target development tasking against VEOs. Notably, the formal UAP data fields classify the phenomenon's physical state as 'Plasma' despite no active sensor interrogation being performed and all kinematic parameters being left blank—illustrating how field-level classification categories can outrun actual observational data. The aircrew's explicit ruling out of a laser attack reflects post-2022 DoD guidance requiring reporters to consider directed-energy explanations before logging an anomaly.

key_findings.finding: The UAP manifested as multiple distinct light and glare events over a 45-minute window at different angles and positions, not a single discrete sighting—with separate observations recorded at five specific timestamps.

quotes.text: FROM 1559Z-1644Z, (b)(1)1.4a OBSERVED MULTIPLE GLARES OR LIGHT FROM UNKNOWN ORIGIN AT DIFFERENT ANGLES AND DIRECTIONS. AT 1559Z, 1602Z AND AT 1644Z, OBSERVED 1X LIGHT/GLARE CROSSED DIRECTLY ON THE FMV CAMERA. AT 1609Z AND 1620Z, (b)(1)1.4a OBSERVED A LIGHT/GLARE HALO EFFECT AT THE TOP OF (b)(1)1.4a FMV FEED.

key_findings.finding: The narrative description of the UAP as a 'misshapen and uneven ball of white light' is categorized in the formal data fields as 'Plasma'—a specific physical-state classification entered despite no sensor return or measurement data supporting it.

quotes.text: MISHAPEN AND UNEVEN BALL OF WHITE LIGHT.

key_findings.finding: No active sensor interrogation of the UAP was attempted, and all kinematic parameters—altitude, depth, velocity, and trajectory—were left blank with 'Estimated' accuracy ratings, meaning no measured data on the object's own movement was obtained.

key_findings.finding: The reporting platform was an AFSOC special operations ISR asset from the 12th Special Operations Squadron (27 SOW) conducting target development against violent extremist organizations under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, logging over 20 hours of total mission time and 14 hours of FMV collection.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document was formally approved for release to AARO and structured using AARO's standardized UAP incident reporting fields, demonstrating AARO's role as the designated recipient of operational UAP reports from USCENTCOM.
The document carries a SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY classification caveat on every page, indicating it was authorized for sharing with Five Eyes partner intelligence services.
